Execution is the process of carrying out a death sentence as a punishment for a crime. Historically, methods have included hanging, beheading, firing squad, electrocution, and lethal injection in various regions and time periods. Modern execution methods aim to minimize suffering and are often carried out under strict legal and medical supervision.

An execution is the carrying out of a death sentence imposed by a court as a punishment for a criminal offense. It is a legal process in which a person is put to death, typically through methods such as hanging, electrocution, lethal injection, or firing squad. Executions are controversial and have been abolished in many countries due to human rights concerns.
